poster_title: Tree Search for LLM Agent Reinforcement Learning
authors: Yuxiang Ji, Ziyu Ma, Yong Wang, Guanhua Chen, Xiangxiang Chu, Liaoni Wu
paper_info: Xiamen University, AMAP, Alibaba Group, Southern University of Science and Technology, 2025

panels.headline: Addressing heavy budget and sparse supervision in multi-turn agent tasks
content: RL has enhanced LLMs' agentic capabilities in single-turn tasks.
Multi-turn tasks in dynamic environments are crucial for next-gen foundation models.
Tree-GRPO aims to optimize budget and supervision in multi-turn RL.

panels.headline: High cost and sparse supervision in multi-turn RL
content: LLM rollouts in multi-turn tasks require significant budget.
Sparse supervision due to reliance on outcome rewards.
Tree-GRPO addresses these challenges with efficient sampling and step-wise supervision.

panels.headline: Tree-GRPO: Tree-based Group Relative Policy Optimization
content: Tree nodes represent complete agent interaction steps.
panels.figure_caption: Overview of the Tree-GRPO training pipeline, showing tree search and group relative advantage estimation.

panels.headline: Evaluated on 11 datasets across various tasks
content: Compared with chain-based methods using different models and scales.

panels.headline: Achieved superior performance with 25% of the rollout budget
content: Reduced rollout budget while maintaining or improving performance.
panels.figure_caption: Comparison of chain-based and tree-based sampling strategies in LLM multi-turn agent RL.

panels.headline: Tree-GRPO enables efficient multi-turn agent interaction
content: Tree-GRPO effectively addresses heavy budget and sparse supervision in multi-turn RL.
Base models can adopt multi-turn interaction paradigms without supervised fine-tuning.
Future work: Explore Tree-GRPO in more complex environments and tasks.

Fig1.caption: Comparison of chain-based and tree-based sampling strategies in LLM multi-turn agent RL. The tree structure brings two major advantages: (i) less rollout budget (both on tokens and toolcalls); (ii) higher performance.
